Team dossier Operation Loose Ends

Tightie Whities

Tight name. Loose story.

Team color
White
Threat level
Briefs filed, dignity pending
Catnip & Hairball
7 hairballs · 3 catnip

Known for

  • Two dogs, two walks, and a very awkward 'how long have you had it?' (PNN-003).
  • Being the target of the most obvious prank in the history of obvious pranks (PNN-005).
  • Having a pair of scorched satin bloomers named in their honor.
  • A team name that practically volunteers.

The file

The Tightie Whities named their team after underwear and then, remarkably, acted surprised. Anyone who names a team that way has pre-approved the joke. The Pyro Posse took the invitation literally and hung a clothesline of laundry on their walk. Then they lit it.

The garment in question was a pair of white satin bloomers. They are not tight. After treatment, they are not white. The charring ran down the middle in a pattern a banner on the same line called 'The Skidmark Synod.' PNN did not name it. PNN would have fought for the word 'Synod' to be somewhere else.

Earlier, in PNN-003, the Whities were spotted walking dogs downhill a few minutes apart. When a neighbor asked how long one member had owned a dog, the answer was a pause. PNN has not recovered from the pause. Clueso filed it as Operation Loose End and has refused to elaborate.

The team has a tight name, a loose story, and a gift for being the one everyone notices. In fairness, that is the right gift for a team named after underwear: you cannot go unnoticed. You can only be uncovered.

Strengths

  • Absolute commitment to the premise.
  • A name that sells itself.
  • Two dogs, apparently.

Weaknesses

  • Follow-up questions.
  • Open flames.
  • The word 'loose,' which has followed them everywhere.

Clueso's advice

Rehearse saying 'about two years.' Then buy a lock for the clothesline.

— Inspector Clueso, PNN
